newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - sign of building sector results recovery?
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - sign of building sector results recovery?

text.p: Next week sees a rash of construction and building material company results, with the broad issues of interest being the state of recovery in the sickly continental European markets, the impact of strong sterling and evidence of the long-awaited UK upturn.
The major players reporting final results are Blue Circle Plc on Monday, Taylor Woodrow Plc on Tuesday, Caradon Plc on Wednesday, Redland Plc and AMEC Plc on Thursday.
First off the block next week is building materials group Blue Circle, which reports its final results. Analysts' pretax profit forecasts range between 295 million stg and 310 million.

Profits for the previous year were 272.8 million, after accounting for exceptional hits of 55 million and 8.3 million for the heating and bathroom units, which were offset by a 54.3 million gain from the sale of a UK landfill unit.
The dividend is seen at between 13.1 pence and 13.3 pence per share versus 12.5 pence in 1995.
Simon Brown at UBS said he would be looking for evidence of how its expansion into South East Asia and Chile was progressing.

Another analyst added that he would be interested in how the U.S. business was performing and Blue Circle's view on interest rate concerns, summing up that the figures would be "a quality performance, but nothing sparkling."

Construction to property development and housing group Taylor Woodrow, is forecast to return 1996 profits of between 63.3 million and 65 million stg against 46 million in 1995. The dividend is seen at between 3.3 pence and 3.5 pence compared to 3.0 pence in 1995.
Mike Betts at Goldman Sachs said he expected the results to show a "continuing positive position," benefiting from an uptick in construction in the UK.

The strong pick-up in housing at home should be another positive factor and although zooming land price inflation remains a worry the group's diverse business spread will leave it less exposed than housebuilder specialists, said Betts.

Building materials group Caradon's year pretax profits are seen between 168 million and 180 million stg compared to 114.3 million in 1995. The dividend payout is seen being pitched between 9.5 pence and 10 pence, compared to 9.5 pence in 1995. It should benefit from a better UK housing market and give a positive short term outlook, said Betts.

Another analyst said Caradon had held up against poor European markets better than others in the sector and would be interested to see if that continued. The group was upbeat at the half year stage, stating it was benefiting from new products and cost cutting measures feeding through.

Redland Plc, the building materials group, is seen returning profits of between 212 million to 261 million stg versus a post-exceptional 273.2 million. The pre-exceptional profit figure for 1995 was 355 million.
The dividend payout is expected to be between 16.7 and 17 pence versus 16.7 pence in 1995.

The key issues for Redland will be the state of the German market, which acocunts for almost half of its sales and a sizeable chunk of profits. Some analysts will also be looking for comment on whether the company will consider spinning off its aggregates business -- which was hinted at privately in recent months as a way of improving returns to shareholders.
It also warned last year that sterling was causing some pain, but analysts say this is already factored into the shareprice.

Lastly, building group AMEC is expected to turn in profits of between 35 and 38 million stg versus 15.9 million the previous year. The dividend is expected to be pitched between 3.0 and 3.3 pence per share.
